title: mos.error.v1
description: Failure envelope for any mos one-shot operation that produced no observation. Routes to stdout (not stderr) so a single `mos --json | jq` pipeline can read both success and failure envelopes; stderr carries the human-readable diagnostic in parallel. The bsd field is conditional — present only when a handle was open at the time of failure (partial-failure path), absent when the failure preceded handle acquisition (pure-open-failure path).

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node (/dev/diskN) of the drive a handle was open against when the failure occurred. Absent when the failure occurred before handle acquisition (e.g. drive not present at all).

exit_code.description: sysexits.h exit code that the process will return. Mirrors the kernel-visible exit and is intended for consumers that read JSON without also gating on $?.

code.description: Stable string contract for programmatic pattern-matching. The set is pinned in include/mos.h alongside the mos_error enum. 'ok' is deliberately excluded — an error envelope reporting code=ok is internally contradictory; success cases route to mos.state.v1 / mos.list.v1 instead. (Previously this enum included 'ok'; that was a schema bug, not an emitter behavior — the CLI never produces error envelopes with code=ok. Removed in v0.3.1-dev. Same as mos.event.v1::error.code.)

message.description: Opaque human-readable text from mos_error_description. Do not pattern-match on this; pattern-match on `code` instead.

context.description: What mos was attempting when the failure occurred (e.g. "could not open drive"). Human-readable; opaque for pattern matching.

recoverable.description: Hint for consuming adapters: true means the error typically clears on retry within seconds (BUSY, TIMEOUT, EXCLUSIVE_ACCESS); false means it won't clear without external action.
